Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

aemo 0.4.3

Bug-fix release. Most queries for data more than about two days old failed, the download cache never worked, aemo_bids() failed for every date and aemo_mlf() outside July. Live tests that would have shown this were being skipped.

Queries older than two days work again

NEMweb now keeps the five-minute files in its Current directory for only about two days; the package assumed 30. Any aemo_price(), aemo_demand(), aemo_dispatch_units() or other NEMweb query for a day between two and 30 days ago therefore looked only in Current, found nothing, and stopped with “No NEMweb files matched the requested range”. Older days fell through to the Archive, which failed too (see below). Each day is now read from an Archive rollup when one exists and from Current otherwise, whatever NEMweb’s retention.

  • Archive rollups are zips of zips (a daily DispatchIS rollup holds the day’s 288 five-minute zips). The parser only looked for CSVs at the top level, so every Archive file was skipped as a failed download. Nested zips are now unpacked, and only the inner files inside the requested window are parsed: an hour’s query reads a dozen files, not 288.
  • Weekly Archive rollups (TradingIS, used by interval = "30min") were matched only to the first day they cover. They now count for all seven.
  • The interval ending at 00:00 is now read from the previous day’s rollup, where NEMweb files it.
  • When a range is older than NEMweb holds, the error now gives the earliest date available and points to MMSDM.
  • When some files in a range fail to download, the result was returned with one “Skipping failed download” warning per file, which made an incomplete series easy to miss. There is now a single warning saying how many files are missing and that the result lacks those intervals (class aemo_partial_download); if every download fails the error has class aemo_download_error.

Bids

  • aemo_bids() failed for every date with “arguments imply differing number of rows: 0, 1”. Its default resolution = "day" (and "joined") read Next_Day_Offer_Energy, which AEMO has emptied in favour of Next_Day_Offer_Energy_SPARSE, and listing an empty NEMweb folder crashed aemo_nemweb_ls(). Day bids are now read from Bidmove_Complete, which carries both BIDDAYOFFER_D and BIDPEROFFER_D, and an empty folder lists as an empty data frame.

  • resolution = "period" returned BIDDAYOFFER_D, the daily table, because it took the first table in each Bidmove_Complete file. It now names BIDPEROFFER_D, and "day" names BIDDAYOFFER_D.

  • Monthly archive rollups named by a single date (PUBLIC_BIDMOVE_COMPLETE_20251002.zip, which holds 2 October to 1 November) were treated as covering that one day, so a request for any other day in the month missed them. A single-date rollup now runs to the next rollup; daily rollups are unaffected.

Marginal loss factors

aemo_mlf() read the newest monthly MMSDM TRANSMISSIONLOSSFACTOR file. Only the June file holds the full determination for the year ahead; the other months carry a few revisions, so outside July the function found too few rows and reported MMSDM as unreachable. Each requested year is now built from its June file and the revisions after it, keeping the latest version of each factor. year = NULL returns the current financial year (previously documented as all years).

The duid filter did nothing, because MMSDM publishes MLFs by connection point and the table has no duid column. DUIDs are now mapped to connection points through aemo_units(), which adds a duid column. The help page also described a bundled fallback table that the function deliberately does not have; it no longer does.

HTTPS

NEMweb now redirects http:// to https://; the package requests https://nemweb.com.au directly.

The cache works

aemo_sha256_file() returned openssl’s "hash" object rather than a plain string, so the integrity check against the stored digest always failed: every cached file was reported as corrupt, deleted and downloaded again. It now returns a plain string. It also closes the file connection it opens, and aemo_parse_csv() no longer opens a text connection per CSV line without closing it.

Tests

The integration tests checked reachability against http://nemweb.com.au, which now redirects to aemo.com.au and returns 403, so they were always skipped; their fixed 2021-2024 dates had also aged out of NEMweb. They now probe the reports directory and use dates relative to today.

aemo 0.4.2

CRAN release: 2026-09-09

Maintenance release fixing a network-dependent test that could fail the package check whenever the NEMweb archive was unreachable.

aemo_fcas_enablement() validated its service argument only after fetching dispatch data, so an unknown service name surfaced the underlying fetch error (for example “NEMweb returned HTTP 403”) rather than the intended “No matching FCAS service columns” message. On check machines that could not reach NEMweb this broke the bad-service-name test in test-dispatch.R, producing an intermittent R CMD check ERROR on the flavours where the archive happened to be unreachable.

The service argument is now validated before any network request, so a bad name fails fast and offline. No change for valid calls.

aemo 0.4.1

CRAN release: 2026-05-27

Maintenance release fixing a test-suite issue reported by CRAN on 2026-05-27. The aemo_units() integration test made a live MMSDM request without a skip_on_cran() guard, so it raised an error on CRAN check machines whenever the NEMweb archive was unreachable. The test is now guarded like the other network-dependent tests and split into a gated live check and an offline-abort check that verifies the no-fallback behaviour. No user-facing code changes.

aemo 0.4.0

CRAN release: 2026-04-28

First release under new maintainership. Reclaims the archived aemo package name (Imanuel Costigan, 2014-2020, v0.1.0 to v0.3.0, archived 2021-12-29). The prior package shipped three functions covering regional prices and demand only; this release is an independent rewrite covering the full NEMweb and MMSDM data surface and shares only the package name.

Version starts at 0.4.0 to sit strictly above the last archived version (0.3.0).

Data functions

Price and demand

  • aemo_price(): 5-min (DISPATCHPRICE) or 30-min (TRADINGPRICE) regional wholesale prices. Pre-5MS (before 2021-10-01) reads TRADINGIS; post-5MS 30-min prices are derived as the arithmetic mean of six 5-min dispatch prices within each trading interval, matching AEMO’s post-5MS TRADINGPRICE derivation.
  • aemo_demand(): regional operational, operational-less-SNSG, or native demand at 5-min resolution.
  • aemo_price_caps(): static reference table of Market Price Cap, Floor, CPT, and APC by financial year. Per-row source citations to the specific AEMC determination.

Dispatch and flow

  • aemo_dispatch_units(): per-DUID generator output at 5-min. measure = "scada_mw" (default) returns SCADA actual; "target_mw" returns DISPATCHLOAD TOTALCLEARED; "both" returns INITIALMW + TOTALCLEARED + SCADAVALUE paired, enabling ramp-trajectory research.
  • aemo_interconnector(): NEM interconnector flows.
  • aemo_rooftop_pv(): estimated rooftop PV actual or forecast.
  • aemo_fcas(), aemo_fcas_enablement(): FCAS prices and enablement across the ten services live since 9 Oct 2023.
  • aemo_constraints(): binding transmission and system constraints with shadow prices.
  • aemo_gencon(): GENCONDATA constraint equations.
  • aemo_spd_constraints(): SPD constraint coefficient tables (SPDREGIONCONSTRAINT, SPDINTERCONNECTORCONSTRAINT, SPDCONNECTIONPOINTCONSTRAINT). Required for nempy-style dispatch replication (Gorman et al. 2022 JOSS 7(70) 3596).
  • aemo_outages(): NETWORK_OUTAGEDETAIL.
  • aemo_market_notices(): MARKETNOTICEDATA feed (LOR, RERT, interventions, suspensions). Pairs with the above for market- event forensics (Rangarajan et al. 2025, Energy Economics 141).

Bids and forecasts

  • aemo_bids(): generator bid stack. resolution = "day" (BIDDAYOFFER_D), "period" (BIDPEROFFER_D), or "joined" (the two inner-joined on (duid, settlementdate, bidtype) so price bands and volumes are accessible together).
  • aemo_predispatch(): P5MIN or PREDISPATCH forecasts. Pass run_datetime to pin a specific forecast vintage (required for forecast-error research; mirrors NEMSEER’s workflow, Prakash 2023 JOSS 8(92) 5883).
  • aemo_pasa(): short-term or medium-term projected assessment of system adequacy. Default windows are horizon-aware.

Gas

  • aemo_gas(): STTM and DWGM.

Reference and settlement

  • aemo_units(): DUID registry. as_of argument performs an effective-date join on DUDETAILSUMMARY so historical queries see the registry as it was at any point in time (e.g. Liddell’s DUIDs pre-2023 retirement).
  • aemo_participants(): PARTICIPANT + DUDETAILSUMMARY.
  • aemo_regions(), aemo_interconnectors(): static metadata.
  • aemo_mlf(), aemo_dlf(): marginal and distribution loss factors from MMSDM.
  • aemo_settlement(): SETCFM (energy cashflow), SETFCASREGIONRECOVERY (FCAS recovery), and SETRESIDUECONTRACTPAYMENT (settlement residues) for gentailer reconciliation workflows.

Reproducibility

  • aemo_snapshot(): returns a provenance record (source URL, SHA-256 of the table body, row count, retrieved-at timestamp) suitable for Zenodo deposit or paper appendix.

Low-level access and configuration

  • aemo_nemweb_ls(), aemo_nemweb_download(): escape hatches for arbitrary NEMweb paths.
  • aemo_cache_info(), aemo_clear_cache(), aemo_throttle().

Conventions

  • All timestamps are POSIXct in Australia/Brisbane (AEST, UTC+10, no DST). NER cl. 2.2.6. Using Australia/Sydney would silently shift every summer interval by one hour.
  • Period-ending timestamps throughout.
  • intervention = FALSE (default) filters DISPATCHPRICE to the market pricing run (INTERVENTION = 0) used in settlement. Pass intervention = TRUE for intervention runs (e.g. the June 2022 NEM suspension).
  • options("aemo.base_url") and options("aemo.mmsdm_base") override the NEMweb host endpoints, supporting the 30 April 2026 NEMweb URL migration without a reinstall.

Data source

Data is published by AEMO at http://nemweb.com.au under the AEMO Copyright Permissions Notice https://www.aemo.com.au/privacy-and-legal-notices/copyright-permissions. Downloads are cached to tools::R_user_dir("aemo", "cache") on first use, with SHA-256 content verification on reuse.
